title: ANALOG-X Earth candidate discovery seeds
scope_note: This is a curated, evidence-linked candidate seed set for reproducible screening, not a complete global search and not a claim that any site is a newly discovered or validated planetary analog. Locations are study-area reference points, not field boundaries or access permissions.
discovery_rules: Separate well-known analog references from under-characterized candidate leads.
Use the planetary mission and process as the unit of comparison, not visual resemblance alone.
Display only measured variables with source, date, units, spatial support and quality warnings.
Do not interpret spectral indices as mineral identification, glacier outlines or brine confirmation.
Treat a candidate recommendation as a research lead until ground-truthed and reviewed by domain specialists.

candidate_sites.name: Chagai small salt playas near Nok Kundi
candidate_sites.hypothesis: A pair of small salt-surfaced playas described southwest of Nok Kundi may offer a focused Pakistan field site for studying evaporite accumulation, sediment transport and dry-playa surface mapping relevant to selected Martian sedimentary-process questions.

evidence_status.historical_geologic_context: NASA technical report identifies two small salt-surfaced playas and discusses potential evaporite/brine context
evidence_status.sentinel2: Queued for STAC search and spectral screening

candidate_sites.coordinate_method: Reference point is the midpoint of two coordinate locations printed in the NASA report (28°35′ N, 62°36′ E and 28°35′ N, 62°40′ E). The displayed bounding box is an analyst-defined search window, not a measured playa polygon.

source_references.title: Playas and possible related saline deposits
source_references.supports: Historical report describes two small salt-surfaced playas at the stated coordinates and discusses possible evaporite/brine sources; it does not provide modern site validation or a current mineral map.

non_transferable: Earth's atmosphere and hydrologic cycle differ from Mars
A surface salt signature does not establish subsurface brine or present-day liquid water
No mineral chemistry, depth profile, surface strength or dust transport data are yet available

candidate_sites.name: Hamun-i-Mashkel playa / Kharan Basin
candidate_sites.hypothesis: The closed Kharan drainage basin and mostly dry Hamun-i-Mashkel playa may provide a process analogue for investigating evaporite accumulation and repeated wetting-drying sedimentary settings on Mars.

evidence_status.historical_geologic_context: NASA report describes the playa and regional sand-transport/salinity context; basin-level facts require current local verification
evidence_status.sentinel2: Queued for STAC search and spectral screening

candidate_sites.coordinate_method: Approximate place-reference coordinate used for data discovery; not a playa boundary. Confirm the AOI against a current hydrology/landform map before field use.

source_references.title: Playas and possible related saline deposits
Hamun-i-Mashkel lake-bed reference
source_references.supports: Approximate point location only; not scientific landform boundary or material classification.

non_transferable: An intermittent Earth playa is not a Martian climate replica
Surface reflectance cannot prove brine chemistry
No long-term inundation sequence or subsurface profile is included yet

candidate_sites.name: Koh-i-Sultan / Chagai
candidate_sites.hypothesis: Useful for volcanic-process field rehearsal; the mapped andesitic/tuff/agglomerate geology is not a basaltic composition match to Syrtis Major.
candidate_sites.coordinate_method: Existing study reference point; not a field boundary.

source_references.title: Chagai Hills area geology, West Pakistan

non_transferable: No verified site mineral map or ground samples
Earth atmosphere, gravity and radiation differ from Mars

candidate_sites.name: Hispar Glacier / Karakoram
candidate_sites.hypothesis: Useful for cryosphere image interpretation, debris-boundary observation and cold-region instrument practice; it does not reproduce lunar permanently shadowed regions or the Martian atmosphere.
candidate_sites.coordinate_method: Approximate gazetteer reference point, not an official glacier centroid or field-access point.

source_references.title: Pakistan Glacier Inventory project
source_references.supports: Existing regional inventory baseline; cite prior work rather than claim national glacier discovery.

non_transferable: No lunar vacuum or permanently shadowed illumination regime
Glacier snow/ice does not establish lunar volatile accessibility
Field access and safety need specialist assessment
